To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The influence of turbulent events on sediment resuspensions under unidirectional flow was investigated using an acoustic Doppler velocimetry technique.

the contribution of turbulent bursts to sediment flux remained identical in conditions above and beneath critical velocity; ejection and sweep were responsible for most sediment transport; and wavelet transform revealed that momentum and sediment flux are correlated in both conditions.

1. the contribution of bursting events to resuspension remained constant above and below the critical velocity; 2. the contribution of the ejection and sweep phases of bursting events to the total sediment transport was greater than the contribution of the up-acceleration or down-deceleration phases of the bursting events; and 2. the momentum of the bursting events was correlated with sediment transport in both test conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the turbulent bursting phenomenon and the initiation of sediment motion under unidirectional flow conditions.
the influence of turbulent bursting and the role of the instantaneous sediment flux on the initiation of sediment motion under unidirectional flows.
the role of turbulent bursting events on sediment entrainment under unidirectional current.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
turbulent bursting is a key mechanism for sediment entrainment.
the bursting phenomenon is the main mechanism for the initiation of incipient motion.
the turbulent bursting events were the most important factor for incipient sediment motion and the initiation of sediment resuspension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the turbulence structure in the near bed flow field plays a significant role in the initiation of sediment motion.
the critical velocity should not be considered as an instantaneous value.

the turbulent bursting phenomenon, which occurs within a turbulent boundary layer, is the main mechanism for incipient sediment motion and that a single critical velocity is not an accurate parameter for predicting the incipient motion of sediment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
turbulent bursting events, and in particular the sweep and ejection events, are the primary drivers of sediment resuspension.
the critical velocity for sediment entrainment should be redefined to account for turbulent fluctuations, which are the primary cause of the sediment entrainment.
the role of turbulence in sediment resuspension should be further investigated.
